It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Gongen-san |rank=旧{{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}・{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} |established=8th year of Emperor Ingyō |札所等={{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道}} No. 5 (Wakayama No. 5) |festival=[[July 24]]・[[July 25]] ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭}}) |map=Japan Wakayama#Japan |main hall=[[Kasuga-zukuri]] (main hall, Upper Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall), Four-Bay Flowing Style (Middle Hall, Lower Hall) Hip-and-Gable Roof (Western Hall) }} [[File:石園坐多久虫玉神社 大和高田市片塩町 Isono-ni-masu-takumushitama-jinja 2013.8.16 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|鳥居]] '''Tōkei Shrine''' (とうけいじんじゃ){{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}. It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). {{出典の明記|date=2017年8月28日 (月) 09:10 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name=Tōkei Shrine |location={{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市}} Higashi 1-1 |image=[[File:Tokei shrine torii.jpg|250px|鳥居]]
{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=250}} |ISO=JP-30 |緯度度=33|緯度分=43|緯度秒=46.93 |経度度=135|経度分=23|経度秒=2.08 |deity=Kumano Sansho Gongen |alternative name=Tōkei Shrine
Tanabe no Miya
Shinkumano
Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen
Gongen-san |rank=旧{{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}・{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} |established=8th year of Emperor Ingyō |札所等={{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道}} No. 5 (Wakayama No. 5) |festival=[[July 24]]・[[July 25]] ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭}}) |map=Japan Wakayama#Japan |main hall=[[Kasuga-zukuri]] (main hall, Upper Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall), Four-Bay Flowing Style (Middle Hall, Lower Hall) Hip-and-Gable Roof (Western Hall) }} [[File:石園坐多久虫玉神社 大和高田市片塩町 Isono-ni-masu-takumushitama-jinja 2013.8.16 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|鳥居]] '''Tōkei Shrine''' (とうけいじんじゃ){{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}. It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Kumano style. * Western Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). * Upper Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the early Edo period. Kumano style. * Middle Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Lower Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Yaoyorozu Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Worship Hall * Fujikura Shrine - deity: Ando Naotsugu. The first lord of the Tanabe Domain and an attached vassal of the Kishu Domain. * Tamaki Shrine - deity: Teokihohiru-no-Mikoto * Niwatori Hime Benzaiten Shrine - deity: Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto * Ebisu Daikoku Shrine - Deities: Ebisu, Daikokuten * Benkei Shrine - deity: Musashibo Benkei * Shrine Office * Statues of Tanza and Benkei * Branch Shrines ** Inari Shrine ** Yasaka Shrine ** Ebisu Shrine ** Benten Shrine ** Urayasu Shrine File:Tokei shrine Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Tokei shrine Nishi.jpg|Western Hall File:Tokei shrine 1.jpg|Shrine buildings (from the front: Middle Hall, Upper Hall, main hall, Western Hall) File:Tokei shrine 2.jpg|Shrine buildings (from the front: Middle Hall, Lower Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall) File:Tokei shrine ookusu.jpg|Large camphor tree File:Tokei jinja kumano tanzou.JPG|Statues of Tanza and Benkei == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties === * Tōkei Shrine 6 Buildings (Buildings) ** Details are as follows. Designated as tangible cultural properties of Wakayama Prefecture on March 17, 2000 (Heisei 21){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Buildings|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014}}, and designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan on February 23, 2017 (Heisei 29)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 17, February 23, 2017.. ** main hall (Shōseidō) ** Western Hall ** Upper Hall ** Middle Hall ** Lower Hall ** Yaoyorozu Hall === National Historic Site === * Part of the historic site "Kumano Kodo" (additional designation on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|accessdate=May 20, 2016}}. === National Place of Scenic Beauty === * Part of the scenic beauty "Landscape of Southern Mandala" (designated on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=May 21, 2016}}. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Mandai-ki 1 Set - Records from the Muromachi to Edo periods. Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Property (books, designated on March 26, 1963){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Fine Arts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201090648/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html |archivedate=February 1, 2016|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. * Goyotome 42 Volumes - Records from the Edo to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Tanabe Town Ledger 130 Volumes and Town Ledger Quick Reference 8 Volumes - Records from the Momoyama to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala 1 Scroll - Painting. Designated on March 16, 2010. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Historic Site === * Tōkei Shrine Precincts - Designated on March 15, 2002{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=Tōkei Shrine (Shinkumano Tōkei Gongen Shrine) Precincts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. It is located at the western end of a series of small hills extending from the eastern part of the city, with the shrine buildings facing north. On the hillside from the middle to the top of Kariyanoyama behind the shrine, three burial mounds from the late Heian to early Kamakura periods were found, yielding artifacts such as jars, sutra cylinders, small boxes, knives, small inkstones, and ancient coins{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=Tōkei Shrine Precincts|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=February 14, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." {{出典の明記|date=2017年8月28日 (月) 09:10 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name=Tōkei Shrine |location={{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市}} Higashi 1-1 |image=[[File:Tokei shrine torii.jpg|250px|鳥居]]

Gongen-san |rank=旧{{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}・{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} |established=8th year of Emperor Ingyō |札所等={{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道}} No. 5 (Wakayama No. 5) |festival=[[July 24]]・[[July 25]] ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭}}) |map=Japan Wakayama#Japan |main hall=[[Kasuga-zukuri]] (main hall, Upper Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall), Four-Bay Flowing Style (Middle Hall, Lower Hall) Hip-and-Gable Roof (Western Hall) }} [[File:石園坐多久虫玉神社 大和高田市片塩町 Isono-ni-masu-takumushitama-jinja 2013.8.16 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|鳥居]] '''Tōkei Shrine''' (とうけいじんじゃ){{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}. It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Kumano style. * Western Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). * Upper Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the early Edo period. Kumano style. * Middle Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Lower Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Yaoyorozu Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Worship Hall * Fujikura Shrine - deity: Ando Naotsugu. The first lord of the Tanabe Domain and an attached vassal of the Kishu Domain. * Tamaki Shrine - deity: Teokihohiru-no-Mikoto * Niwatori Hime Benzaiten Shrine - deity: Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto * Ebisu Daikoku Shrine - Deities: Ebisu, Daikokuten * Benkei Shrine - deity: Musashibo Benkei * Shrine Office * Statues of Tanza and Benkei * Branch Shrines ** Inari Shrine ** Yasaka Shrine ** Ebisu Shrine ** Benten Shrine ** Urayasu Shrine File:Tokei shrine Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Tokei shrine Nishi.jpg|Western Hall File:Tokei shrine 1.jpg|Shrine buildings (from the front: Middle Hall, Upper Hall, main hall, Western Hall) File:Tokei shrine 2.jpg|Shrine buildings (from the front: Middle Hall, Lower Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall) File:Tokei shrine ookusu.jpg|Large camphor tree File:Tokei jinja kumano tanzou.JPG|Statues of Tanza and Benkei == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties === * Tōkei Shrine 6 Buildings (Buildings) ** Details are as follows. Designated as tangible cultural properties of Wakayama Prefecture on March 17, 2000 (Heisei 21){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Buildings|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014}}, and designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan on February 23, 2017 (Heisei 29)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 17, February 23, 2017.. ** main hall (Shōseidō) ** Western Hall ** Upper Hall ** Middle Hall ** Lower Hall ** Yaoyorozu Hall === National Historic Site === * Part of the historic site "Kumano Kodo" (additional designation on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|accessdate=May 20, 2016}}. === National Place of Scenic Beauty === * Part of the scenic beauty "Landscape of Southern Mandala" (designated on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=May 21, 2016}}. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Mandai-ki 1 Set - Records from the Muromachi to Edo periods. Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Property (books, designated on March 26, 1963){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Fine Arts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201090648/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html |archivedate=February 1, 2016|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. * Goyotome 42 Volumes - Records from the Edo to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Tanabe Town Ledger 130 Volumes and Town Ledger Quick Reference 8 Volumes - Records from the Momoyama to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala 1 Scroll - Painting. Designated on March 16, 2010. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Historic Site === * Tōkei Shrine Precincts - Designated on March 15, 2002{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=Tōkei Shrine (Shinkumano Tōkei Gongen Shrine) Precincts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. It is located at the western end of a series of small hills extending from the eastern part of the city, with the shrine buildings facing north. On the hillside from the middle to the top of Kariyanoyama behind the shrine, three burial mounds from the late Heian to early Kamakura periods were found, yielding artifacts such as jars, sutra cylinders, small boxes, knives, small inkstones, and ancient coins{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=Tōkei Shrine Precincts|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=February 14, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." Minakata was married to Matsue, the fourth daughter of the shrine's chief priest, Tamura Sozo. == Events == === festivals === * Ota festival ** April 15 * Summer Purification ceremony ** June 30{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Summer Purification ceremony |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} * festival ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭}}) ** July 24 (Evening) ** July 25 (Main festival) {{main|Tanabe festival}} * Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ** December 31{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} === Other Events === * {{ill|Benkei festival|ja|弁慶まつり}} (A play is performed at Tōkei Shrine on the first day of the festival, based on the legend that Musashibo Benkei was born at the Daifuku-in within the shrine precincts) ** Early October{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} Since October 1986 (Showa 61), the Benkei Market has been held at the Tōkei Shrine horse grounds (Higashi) on the third Sunday of each month to promote local products. In December 2020, the venue was moved to the Kappark at Oginoyama Park{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei Market |publisher=Tanabe Gongen-san |rank=旧{{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}・{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} |established=8th year of Emperor Ingyō |札所等={{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道}} No. 5 (Wakayama No. 5) |festival=[[July 24]]・[[July 25]] ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭}}) |map=Japan Wakayama#Japan |main hall=[[Kasuga-zukuri]] (main hall, Upper Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall), Four-Bay Flowing Style (Middle Hall, Lower Hall) Hip-and-Gable Roof (Western Hall) }} [[File:石園坐多久虫玉神社 大和高田市片塩町 Isono-ni-masu-takumushitama-jinja 2013.8.16 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|鳥居]] '''Tōkei Shrine''' (とうけいじんじゃ){{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}. It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Kumano style. * Western Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). * Upper Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the early Edo period. Kumano style. * Middle Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Lower Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Yaoyorozu Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Worship Hall * Fujikura Shrine - deity: Ando Naotsugu. Designated as tangible cultural properties of Wakayama Prefecture on March 17, 2000 (Heisei 21){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Buildings|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014}}, and designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan on February 23, 2017 (Heisei 29)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 17, February 23, 2017.. ** main hall (Shōseidō) ** Western Hall ** Upper Hall ** Middle Hall ** Lower Hall ** Yaoyorozu Hall === National Historic Site === * Part of the historic site "Kumano Kodo" (additional designation on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|accessdate=May 20, 2016}}. === National Place of Scenic Beauty === * Part of the scenic beauty "Landscape of Southern Mandala" (designated on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=May 21, 2016}}. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Mandai-ki 1 Set - Records from the Muromachi to Edo periods. Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Property (books, designated on March 26, 1963){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Fine Arts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201090648/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html |archivedate=February 1, 2016|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. * Goyotome 42 Volumes - Records from the Edo to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Tanabe Town Ledger 130 Volumes and Town Ledger Quick Reference 8 Volumes - Records from the Momoyama to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala 1 Scroll - Painting. Designated on March 16, 2010. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Historic Site === * Tōkei Shrine Precincts - Designated on March 15, 2002{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=Tōkei Shrine (Shinkumano Tōkei Gongen Shrine) Precincts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. It is located at the western end of a series of small hills extending from the eastern part of the city, with the shrine buildings facing north. On the hillside from the middle to the top of Kariyanoyama behind the shrine, three burial mounds from the late Heian to early Kamakura periods were found, yielding artifacts such as jars, sutra cylinders, small boxes, knives, small inkstones, and ancient coins{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=Tōkei Shrine Precincts|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=February 14, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." Minakata was married to Matsue, the fourth daughter of the shrine's chief priest, Tamura Sozo. == Events == === festivals === * Ota festival ** April 15 * Summer Purification ceremony ** June 30{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Summer Purification ceremony |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} * festival ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭}}) ** July 24 (Evening) ** July 25 (Main festival) {{main|Tanabe festival}} * Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ** December 31{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} === Other Events === * {{ill|Benkei festival|ja|弁慶まつり}} (A play is performed at Tōkei Shrine on the first day of the festival, based on the legend that Musashibo Benkei was born at the Daifuku-in within the shrine precincts) ** Early October{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} Since October 1986 (Showa 61), the Benkei Market has been held at the Tōkei Shrine horse grounds (Higashi) on the third Sunday of each month to promote local products. He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Designated on March 16, 2010. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Historic Site === * Tōkei Shrine Precincts - Designated on March 15, 2002{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=Tōkei Shrine (Shinkumano Tōkei Gongen Shrine) Precincts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). It is located at the western end of a series of small hills extending from the eastern part of the city, with the shrine buildings facing north. On the hillside from the middle to the top of Kariyanoyama behind the shrine, three burial mounds from the late Heian to early Kamakura periods were found, yielding artifacts such as jars, sutra cylinders, small boxes, knives, small inkstones, and ancient coins{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=Tōkei Shrine Precincts|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=February 14, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." Minakata was married to Matsue, the fourth daughter of the shrine's chief priest, Tamura Sozo. == Events == === festivals === * Ota festival ** April 15 * Summer Purification ceremony ** June 30{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Summer Purification ceremony |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} * festival ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭}}) ** July 24 (Evening) ** July 25 (Main festival) {{main|Tanabe festival}} * Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ** December 31{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} === Other Events === * {{ill|Benkei festival|ja|弁慶まつり}} (A play is performed at Tōkei Shrine on the first day of the festival, based on the legend that Musashibo Benkei was born at the Daifuku-in within the shrine precincts) ** Early October{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} Since October 1986 (Showa 61), the Benkei Market has been held at the Tōkei Shrine horse grounds (Higashi) on the third Sunday of each month to promote local products. It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661).
