{{JIS2004|説明=雞}} {{神社 |名称=鬪雞神社 |画像=[[File:Tokei shrine torii.jpg|270px]]
鳥居
{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=270}} |所在地=[[和歌山県]][[田辺市]]東陽1-1 |ISO=JP-30 |緯度度=33|緯度分=43|緯度秒=46.9 |経度度=135|経度分=23|経度秒=2 |祭神=熊野三所神 |別名=闘鶏神社
田辺宮
新熊野
新熊野雞合大権現
権現さん |社格=旧[[県社]]・[[別表神社]] |創建=[[允恭天皇]]8年 |札所等=[[神仏霊場巡拝の道]]第5番（和歌山第5番） |例祭=[[7月24日]]・[[7月25日|25日]]（[[田辺祭]]） |地図=Japan Wakayama#Japan |本殿=春日造（本殿・上殿・八百萬殿）、四間社流造（中殿・下殿）入母屋造（西殿） }} '''鬪雞神社'''（とうけいじんじゃ）{{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}}は、[[和歌山県]][[田辺市]]にある[[神社]]。史跡（和歌山県指定文化財）の名称としては「鬪雞神社」となっているが、[[宗教法人]]の名称としては漢字に「鳥」の入った「鬪鷄神社」である[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf 和歌山県報第2243号（9頁）] 和歌山県、2023-06-18閲覧。「闘鶏神社」などとも表記される。旧称は'''田辺宮'''、'''新熊野'''、'''新熊野雞合大権現'''。通称：権現さん。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === [[允恭天皇]]8年（[[419年]]）9月に[[分霊#勧請|勧請]]したとされるが、創建時の神社の歴史はよくわかっていない[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf 鬪雞神社の歴史と文化] 田辺市立田辺歴史民俗資料館、2023-06-18閲覧[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf 文化財センター季刊情報誌 風車 紀州の歴史と文化の風] 公益財団法人和歌山県文化財センター、2023-06-18閲覧。一方、天武天皇の時代の[[684年]]に建立されたとする記録も残る。また、[[田辺湾]]の[[神島 (和歌山県)|神島]]に神光が上がり、まず仮庵山（社殿南側にある山）に降り立ち、しばらくして龍仙山へ移りさらに天に上っていったという龍神信仰も残っている。以上から龍神信仰を元にした自然崇拝の祭祀の場所が次第に整えられたものとみられる。 === 中近世 === 『[[紀伊続風土記]]』や江戸時代の古文書によると、12世紀前半に[[熊野別当]]・[[湛快]]のときに熊野三所権現を勧請した。そして熊野別当家によって聖地として整備され「新熊野権現社」と称されるようになった。 社名は『[[平家物語]]』の故事（鶏合わせ神事）に由来している。『平家物語』などによれば、[[治承・寿永の乱]]（源平合戦）の時、熊野別当・[[湛増]]は社地の[[ニワトリ|鶏]]を紅白2色に分けて闘わせ、白の鶏が勝ったことから[[源氏]]に味方することを決め『平家物語』鶏合わせ（[[壇ノ浦の戦い|壇ノ浦合戦]]）のくだり、[[熊野水軍]]を率いて[[壇ノ浦]]へ出陣したという。この『平家物語』の故事から中世には「鶏合大権現」「鶏合宮」「鬪雞宮」とも称された。 鬪雞神社のある地は[[西国三十三所|西国三十三カ所巡礼]]の第一番札所の那智山寺（[[青岸渡寺]]）から第二番札所の[[紀三井寺]]までの中継地で、中世以降は参詣道や巡礼路の要衝となった。 しかし、15世紀末以降に二度の戦乱による焼失（明応年間及び天正年間）で荒廃し、完全な再建まで約150年を要した。慶長5年（1600年）に田辺領主となった浅野左衛門佐は新熊野権現の再興を図った。紀州徳川家の統治後は紀州藩付家老の安藤家の所領となり、元和5年（1619年）に[[安藤直次]]が田辺領主となった後は町衆からの深い信仰も集めて神社は再興を果たした。 === 近現代 === [[明治]]の[[神仏分離]]の際に「'''鬪雞神社'''」を正式な社名とした。 [[1871年]]（明治4年）に郷社（田辺県）、[[1873年]]（明治6年）に村社（和歌山県）、[[1881年]]（明治14年）2月には[[県社]]となっている。 [[1915年]]（[[大正]]4年）7月19日、[[朝香宮鳩彦王]]が御成毛利柴庵『皇室と紀伊』（1935年）346頁。。 [[1971年]]（[[昭和]]46年）7月に[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に加列されている。 [[2016年]]（[[平成]]28年）[[10月23日]]、[[第40回世界遺産委員会]]継続会議において、[[文化遺産 (世界遺産)|世界文化遺産]]「[[紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道]]」に追加登録された[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more 世界遺産への追加登録承認　闘鶏神社や八上王子跡など]紀伊民報 2016年6月11日。 なお[[プロ野球]]の独立リーグ、BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE（現・[[関西独立リーグ (2代目)]]）に[[2017年]]（[[平成]]29年）より加盟した和歌山ファイティングバーズ（現・[[和歌山ウェイブス]]）はこの神社が名の由来だった{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = 野球で地域盛り上げたい 田辺市に独立リーグ球団 | publisher = [[紀伊民報]] | date = 2016-06-10 | accessdate = 2016-06-26 }}。 == 熊野神社としての重要性 == 現存する社殿は近世の再建に係る6棟が揃って遺存するもので、仮庵山を背に北面して建ち、東より西へ西殿、本殿、上殿、中殿、下殿、八百萬殿の6棟が横一列に並ぶ。 建立年代は上殿が最も古く明暦4年（万治元年、1658年）に氏子衆によって建てられた。次いで上殿東側に本殿が[[寛文]]元年（[[1661年]]）に[[安藤直清]]によって寄進された。それから数十年後の[[元文]]2年（[[1737年]]）に本殿東側に西殿が再建された。さらに上殿西側の中殿（中四社）、下殿（下四社）、八百萬殿（満山宮）が[[延享]]5年（[[1748年]]）に再建されて社殿群6棟が揃った。本殿（證誠殿）と上殿（西御前）の配置は熊野本宮大社と共通しており、本殿の祭神が伊邪那美命である点が異なるが、当社には『那智参詣曼荼羅』が伝わるなど熊野との強い関係性を示している。 本殿と上殿は一間社[[春日造]]かつ奥行二間とする、いわゆる熊野造で田辺地方における数少ない17世紀中期以前に遡る貴重な神社建築例である。各棟ともに細部には地域的特色を備え、近世における当地方の神社建築の展開を考えるうえでも貴重な遺構とされる{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=鬪雞神社/６棟|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ わかやま文化財ガイド]|publisher=和歌山県|accessdate=2015-02-14}}。これらの社殿は国の重要文化財に指定されている。 == 祭神 == 社殿は6棟あり、それぞれ以下の神を祀る。 * 本殿 - 祭神：[[イザナミ|伊邪那美命]] * 西殿 - 祭神：速玉之男命、事解之男神 * 上殿 - 祭神：[[イザナギ|伊邪那岐命]]、[[天照大神|天照皇大神]]、[[ウカノミタマ|宇賀御魂命]] * 中殿 - 祭神：[[ニニギ|瓊々杵尊命]]、[[ウガヤフキアエズ|鵜葺草葺不合命]]、[[ホオリ|火々出見尊]]、[[アメノオシホミミ|天之忍穂耳命]] * 下殿 - 祭神：[[カグツチ|火産霊命]]、[[ミヅハノメ|弥都波能売命]]、[[ワクムスビ|稚産霊命]]、[[ハニヤス|埴山比売命]] * 八百萬殿 - 祭神：[[アメノタヂカラオ|手力男命]]、[[八百万の神|八百万神]] == 境内 == * 本殿（證誠殿、[[重要文化財]]） - [[寛文]]元年（[[1661年]]）建。熊野造。 * 西殿（重要文化財） - [[元文]]2年（[[1737年]]）建。 * 上殿（重要文化財） - 江戸時代前期建。熊野造。 * 中殿（重要文化財） - [[延享]]5年（[[1748年]]）建。 * 下殿（重要文化財） - 延享5年（1748年）建。 * 八百萬殿（重要文化財） - 延享5年（1748年）建。 * 拝殿 * 藤厳神社 - 祭神：[[安藤直次]]。[[紀伊田辺藩]]初代藩主で[[紀州藩]][[御附家老|附家老]]。 * 玉置神社 - 祭神：手置帆負命 * 雞姫弁財天社 - 祭神：[[イチキシマヒメ|市杵島姫命]] * 戎大黒神社 - 祭神：[[えびす|恵比寿]]、[[大黒天]] * 弁慶社 - 祭神：[[武蔵坊弁慶]] * 社務所 * 湛増・弁慶の像 * 境外社 ** [[稲荷神社]] ** [[八坂神社]] ** [[えびす神社|恵比須神社]] ** 弁天神社 ** 浦安神社 File:Tokei shrine Haiden.jpg|拝殿 File:Tokei shrine Nishi.jpg|西殿 File:Tokei shrine 1.jpg|社殿（手前から中殿・上殿・本殿・西殿） File:Tokei shrine 2.jpg|社殿（手前から中殿・下殿・八百萬殿） File:Tokei shrine ookusu.jpg|大楠 File:Tokei jinja kumano tanzou.JPG|湛増と弁慶の像 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財 === * 闘雞神社 6棟（建造物） *: 内訳は以下。[[2000年]]（[[平成]]21年）3月17日に「鬪雞神社 6棟」として和歌山県指定の[[有形文化財]]に指定されたのち{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=県指定文化財・有形文化財・建造物|publisher=和歌山県教育委員会|accessdate=2014-02-14}}、[[2017年]]（平成29年）2月23日に国の[[重要文化財]]に指定平成29年2月23日文部科学省告示第17号。。 ** 本殿（證誠殿） ** 西殿 ** 上殿 ** 中殿 ** 下殿 ** 八百萬殿 === 国の史跡 === * 史跡「[[熊野古道|熊野参詣道]]」の一部（[[2015年]]〈平成27年〉10月7日、追加指定）{{Cite web|和書|publisher=田辺市教育委員会|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=田辺市の指定文化財一覧表|accessdate=2016-05-20}}。 === 国の名勝 === * 名勝「南方曼荼羅の風景地」の一部（2015年〈平成27年〉10月7日指定）{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=田辺市の指定文化財一覧表|publisher=田辺市教育委員会|accessdate=2016-05-21}}。 === 和歌山県指定有形文化財 === * 万代記 1括 - 室町から江戸の記録。和歌山県指定有形文化財（書籍、[[1963年]]〈昭和38年〉3月26日指定）{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html|title=県指定文化財・有形文化財・美術工芸品|publisher=和歌山県教育委員会|accessdate=2014-02-14|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201090648/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html |archivedate=2016-02-01|url-status=dead|url-status-date=2019-07}}。 * 御用留 42冊 - 江戸時代から近代の記録（書籍、[[1970年]]〈昭和45年〉5月25日指定）。 * 田辺町大帳 130冊および町大帳早引 8冊 - 桃山～近代の記録（書籍、1970年〈昭和45年〉5月25日指定）。 * [[那智参詣曼荼羅]] 1幅 - 絵画。[[2010年]]（平成22年）3月16日指定。 === 和歌山県指定史跡 === * 鬪雞神社境内 - [[2002年]]（平成23年）3月15日指定{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=鬪雞神社 （新熊野鬪雞権現社）境内|publisher=和歌山県教育委員会|accessdate=2014-02-14|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=2017-02-23|url-status=dead|url-status-date=2019-07}}。市街の東部に連なる小丘陵の西端、仮庵山の北麓にあり、社殿はほぼ北向きに鎮座している。社殿背後の仮庵山の中腹から山頂で、平安時代末期から鎌倉時代初頭の経塚が3基発見され、外容器の甕、経筒、合子（ごうす）、刀子（とうす）、小型硯、古銭などの遺物が出土した{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=鬪雞神社境内|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ わかやま文化財ガイド]|publisher=和歌山県|accessdate=2015-02-14|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=2017-02-23|url-status=dead|url-status-date=2019-07}}。また、仮庵山については[[南方熊楠]]が「当県で平地にはちょっと見られぬ密林なり」と述べている。熊楠は闘雞神社[[宮司]]田村宗造の四女松枝の夫である。 == 行事 == === 祭事　=== * 御田祭 ** 4月15日 * 夏越大祓式 ** 6月30日{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=夏越大祓式 |publisher=田辺市 |work= 鬪雞神社を知る |accessdate=2020-04-20 }} * 例大祭（[[田辺祭]]） ** 7月24日（宵宮） ** 7月25日（本祭） {{main|田辺祭}} * 年越大祓式・除夜祭 ** 12月31日{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=年越大祓式・除夜祭 |publisher=田辺市 |work= 鬪雞神社を知る |accessdate=2020-04-20 }} === その他の行事　=== * [[弁慶まつり]]（[[武蔵坊弁慶|弁慶]]が鬪鷄神社境内の大福院で産まれたという伝説から、祭り1日目は同神社で演劇が行われる） ** 10月上旬{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=弁慶祭り |publisher=田辺市 |work= 鬪雞神社を知る |accessdate=2020-04-20 }} なお、1986年（昭和61年）10月から地場産品の育成のために鬪雞神社馬場（東陽）で弁慶市（毎月第三日曜日）が開催されていたが、2020年12月から扇ケ浜公園カッパークに会場を移転した{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=弁慶市 |publisher=田辺市 |work= 鬪雞神社を知る |accessdate=2020-04-20 }}[https://www.agara.co.jp/article/281766/ 名物朝市が人気　田辺の「弁慶市」来場者1年で1・6倍に] 紀伊民報、2023-06-18閲覧。 == 氏子町 == {{main|田辺祭#笠鉾・衣笠}} {{main|田辺城#城下町}} * 本町 * 江川町 * 福路町 * 紺屋町 * 片町 * 栄町 * 北新町 * 南新町 * 上屋敷町 * 中屋敷町 * 下屋敷町 * 新屋敷町 * 今福町 * {{出典の明記|date=2017th year 8月28日 (月) 09:10 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name=Tōkei Shrine |location={{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Higashi 1-1 |image=[[File:Tokei shrine torii.jpg|250px|鳥居]]
{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=250}} |ISO=JP-30 |緯度度=33|緯度分=43|緯度秒=46.93 |経度度=135|経度分=23|経度秒=2.08 |deity=Kumano Sansho Gongen |alternative name=Tōkei Shrine
Tanabe no Miya
Shinkumano
Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen
Gongen-san |Rank=旧{{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |established=8th year of Emperor Ingyō |札所等={{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} No. 5 (Wakayama No. 5) |festival=[[July 24]]・[[July 25]] ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |map=Japan Wakayama#Japan |main hall=[[Kasuga-zukuri]] (main hall, Upper Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall), Four-Bay Flowing Style (Middle Hall, Lower Hall) Hip-and-Gable Roof (Western Hall) }} [[File:石園坐多久虫玉神社 大和高田市片塩町 Isono-ni-masu-takumushitama-jinja 2013.8.16 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|鳥居]] '''Tōkei Shrine''' (とうけいじんじゃ){{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine Rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所|1=Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|12=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺|1=Seiganto-ji|12=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Kumano style. * Western Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). * Upper Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the early Edo period. Kumano style. * Middle Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Lower Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Yaoyorozu Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Worship Hall * Fujikura Shrine - deity: Ando Naotsugu. The first lord of the Tanabe Domain and an attached vassal of the Kishu Domain. * Tamaki Shrine - deity: Teokihohiru-no-Mikoto * Niwatori Hime Benzaiten Shrine - deity: Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto * Ebisu Daikoku Shrine - Deities: Ebisu, Daikokuten * Benkei Shrine - deity: Musashibo Benkei * Shrine Office * Statues of Tanza and Benkei * Branch Shrines ** Inari Shrine ** Yasaka Shrine ** Ebisu Shrine ** Benten Shrine ** Urayasu Shrine File:Tokei shrine Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Tokei shrine Nishi.jpg|Western Hall File:Tokei shrine 1.jpg|Shrine buildings (from the front: Middle Hall, Upper Hall, main hall, Western Hall) File:Tokei shrine 2.jpg|Shrine buildings (from the front: Middle Hall, Lower Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall) File:Tokei shrine ookusu.jpg|Large camphor tree File:Tokei jinja kumano tanzou.JPG|Statues of Tanza and Benkei == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties === * Tōkei Shrine 6 Buildings (Buildings) ** Details are as follows. Designated as tangible cultural properties of Wakayama Prefecture on March 17, 2000 (Heisei 21){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Buildings|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014}}, and designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan on February 23, 2017 (Heisei 29)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 17, February 23, 2017.. ** main hall (Shōseidō) ** Western Hall ** Upper Hall ** Middle Hall ** Lower Hall ** Yaoyorozu Hall === National Historic Site === * Part of the historic site "Kumano Kodo" (additional designation on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|accessdate=May 20, 2016}}. === National Place of Scenic Beauty === * Part of the scenic beauty "Landscape of Southern Mandala" (designated on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=May 21, 2016}}. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Mandai-ki 1 Set - Records from the Muromachi to Edo periods. Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Property (books, designated on March 26, 1963){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Fine Arts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201090648/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html |archivedate=February 1, 2016|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. * Goyotome 42 Volumes - Records from the Edo to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Tanabe Town Ledger 130 Volumes and Town Ledger Quick Reference 8 Volumes - Records from the Momoyama to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala 1 Scroll - Painting. Designated on March 16, 2010. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Historic Site === * Tōkei Shrine Precincts - Designated on March 15, 2002{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=Tōkei Shrine (Shinkumano Tōkei Gongen Shrine) Precincts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. It is located at the western end of a series of small hills extending from the eastern part of the city, with the shrine buildings facing north. On the hillside from the middle to the top of Kariyanoyama behind the shrine, three Kofuns from the late Heian to early Kamakura periods were found, yielding artifacts such as jars, sutra cylinders, small boxes, knives, small inkstones, and ancient coins{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=Tōkei Shrine Precincts|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=February 14, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." Minakata was married to Matsue, the fourth daughter of the shrine's chief priest, Tamura Sozo. == Events == === festivals === * Ota festival ** April 15 * Summer Purification ceremony ** June 30{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Summer Purification ceremony |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} * festival ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) ** July 24 (Evening) ** July 25 (Main festival) {{main|Tanabe festival}} * Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ** December 31{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} === Other Events === * {{ill|Benkei festival|ja|弁慶まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (A play is performed at Tōkei Shrine on the first day of the festival, based on the legend that Musashibo Benkei was born at the Daifuku-in within the shrine precincts) ** Early October{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} Since October 1986 (Showa 61), the Benkei Market has been held at the Tōkei Shrine horse grounds (Higashi) on the third Sunday of each month to promote local products. In December 2020, the venue was moved to the Kappark at Oginoyama Park{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei Market |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }}[https://www.agara.co.jp/article/281766/ The famous morning market is popular - The Benkei Market in Tanabe has seen a 1.6-fold increase in visitors in one year] Kii Minpo, viewed June 18, 2023. == Parish Towns == {{main|Tanabe festival#Kasahoko and Kinasa}} {{main|Tanabe Castle#Castle Town}} * Honmachi * Egawacho * Fukurocho * Konyacho * Katamachi * Sakaemachi * Kitashimmachi * Minamishimmachi * Kamiyashikicho * Nakayashikicho * Shimoyashikicho * Arayashikicho * Imafuku * Egawamasugatamachi (Developed as a residential area during the Meiji and Taisho periods with land reclaimed from Egawahamacho) == Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range == : 4 {{ill|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Gongen-san |Rank=旧{{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |established=8th year of Emperor Ingyō |札所等={{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} No. 5 (Wakayama No. 5) |festival=[[July 24]]・[[July 25]] ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |map=Japan Wakayama#Japan |main hall=[[Kasuga-zukuri]] (main hall, Upper Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall), Four-Bay Flowing Style (Middle Hall, Lower Hall) Hip-and-Gable Roof (Western Hall) }} [[File:石園坐多久虫玉神社 大和高田市片塩町 Isono-ni-masu-takumushitama-jinja 2013.8.16 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|鳥居]] '''Tōkei Shrine''' (とうけいじんじゃ){{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine Rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所|1=Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|12=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺|1=Seiganto-ji|12=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Kumano style. * Western Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). * Upper Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the early Edo period. Kumano style. * Middle Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Lower Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Yaoyorozu Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Worship Hall * Fujikura Shrine - deity: Ando Naotsugu. Designated as tangible cultural properties of Wakayama Prefecture on March 17, 2000 (Heisei 21){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Buildings|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014}}, and designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan on February 23, 2017 (Heisei 29)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 17, February 23, 2017.. ** main hall (Shōseidō) ** Western Hall ** Upper Hall ** Middle Hall ** Lower Hall ** Yaoyorozu Hall === National Historic Site === * Part of the historic site "Kumano Kodo" (additional designation on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|accessdate=May 20, 2016}}. === National Place of Scenic Beauty === * Part of the scenic beauty "Landscape of Southern Mandala" (designated on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=May 21, 2016}}. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Mandai-ki 1 Set - Records from the Muromachi to Edo periods. Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Property (books, designated on March 26, 1963){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Fine Arts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201090648/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html |archivedate=February 1, 2016|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. * Goyotome 42 Volumes - Records from the Edo to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Tanabe Town Ledger 130 Volumes and Town Ledger Quick Reference 8 Volumes - Records from the Momoyama to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala 1 Scroll - Painting. Designated on March 16, 2010. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Historic Site === * Tōkei Shrine Precincts - Designated on March 15, 2002{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=Tōkei Shrine (Shinkumano Tōkei Gongen Shrine) Precincts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. It is located at the western end of a series of small hills extending from the eastern part of the city, with the shrine buildings facing north. On the hillside from the middle to the top of Kariyanoyama behind the shrine, three Kofuns from the late Heian to early Kamakura periods were found, yielding artifacts such as jars, sutra cylinders, small boxes, knives, small inkstones, and ancient coins{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=Tōkei Shrine Precincts|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=February 14, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." Minakata was married to Matsue, the fourth daughter of the shrine's chief priest, Tamura Sozo. == Events == === festivals === * Ota festival ** April 15 * Summer Purification ceremony ** June 30{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Summer Purification ceremony |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} * festival ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) ** July 24 (Evening) ** July 25 (Main festival) {{main|Tanabe festival}} * Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ** December 31{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} === Other Events === * {{ill|Benkei festival|ja|弁慶まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (A play is performed at Tōkei Shrine on the first day of the festival, based on the legend that Musashibo Benkei was born at the Daifuku-in within the shrine precincts) ** Early October{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} Since October 1986 (Showa 61), the Benkei Market has been held at the Tōkei Shrine horse grounds (Higashi) on the third Sunday of each month to promote local products. In December 2020, the venue was moved to the Kappark at Oginoyama Park{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei Market |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }}[https://www.agara.co.jp/article/281766/ The famous morning market is popular - The Benkei Market in Tanabe has seen a 1.6-fold increase in visitors in one year] Kii Minpo, viewed June 18, 2023. == Parish Towns == {{main|Tanabe festival#Kasahoko and Kinasa}} {{main|Tanabe Castle#Castle Town}} * Honmachi * Egawacho * Fukurocho * Konyacho * Katamachi * Sakaemachi * Kitashimmachi * Minamishimmachi * Kamiyashikicho * Nakayashikicho * Shimoyashikicho * Arayashikicho * Imafuku * Egawamasugatamachi (Developed as a residential area during the Meiji and Taisho periods with land reclaimed from Egawahamacho) == Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range == : 4 {{ill|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=250}} |ISO=JP-30 |緯度度=33|緯度分=43|緯度秒=46.93 |経度度=135|経度分=23|経度秒=2.08 |deity=Kumano Sansho Gongen |alternative name=Tōkei Shrine
Tanabe no Miya
Shinkumano
Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen
Gongen-san |Rank=旧{{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |established=8th year of Emperor Ingyō |札所等={{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} No. 5 (Wakayama No. 5) |festival=[[July 24]]・[[July 25]] ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |map=Japan Wakayama#Japan |main hall=[[Kasuga-zukuri]] (main hall, Upper Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall), Four-Bay Flowing Style (Middle Hall, Lower Hall) Hip-and-Gable Roof (Western Hall) }} [[File:石園坐多久虫玉神社 大和高田市片塩町 Isono-ni-masu-takumushitama-jinja 2013.8.16 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|鳥居]] '''Tōkei Shrine''' (とうけいじんじゃ){{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|ja|田辺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine Rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所|1=Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|12=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺|1=Seiganto-ji|12=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Kumano style. * Western Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). * Upper Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the early Edo period. Kumano style. * Middle Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Lower Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Yaoyorozu Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Worship Hall * Fujikura Shrine - deity: Ando Naotsugu. The first lord of the Tanabe Domain and an attached vassal of the Kishu Domain. * Tamaki Shrine - deity: Teokihohiru-no-Mikoto * Niwatori Hime Benzaiten Shrine - deity: Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto * Ebisu Daikoku Shrine - Deities: Ebisu, Daikokuten * Benkei Shrine - deity: Musashibo Benkei * Shrine Office * Statues of Tanza and Benkei * Branch Shrines ** Inari Shrine ** Yasaka Shrine ** Ebisu Shrine ** Benten Shrine ** Urayasu Shrine File:Tokei shrine Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Tokei shrine Nishi.jpg|Western Hall File:Tokei shrine 1.jpg|Shrine buildings (from the front: Middle Hall, Upper Hall, main hall, Western Hall) File:Tokei shrine 2.jpg|Shrine buildings (from the front: Middle Hall, Lower Hall, Yaoyorozu Hall) File:Tokei shrine ookusu.jpg|Large camphor tree File:Tokei jinja kumano tanzou.JPG|Statues of Tanza and Benkei == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties === * Tōkei Shrine 6 Buildings (Buildings) ** Details are as follows. Designated as tangible cultural properties of Wakayama Prefecture on March 17, 2000 (Heisei 21){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Buildings|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014}}, and designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan on February 23, 2017 (Heisei 29)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 17, February 23, 2017.. ** main hall (Shōseidō) ** Western Hall ** Upper Hall ** Middle Hall ** Lower Hall ** Yaoyorozu Hall === National Historic Site === * Part of the historic site "Kumano Kodo" (additional designation on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|accessdate=May 20, 2016}}. === National Place of Scenic Beauty === * Part of the scenic beauty "Landscape of Southern Mandala" (designated on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=May 21, 2016}}. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Mandai-ki 1 Set - Records from the Muromachi to Edo periods. Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Property (books, designated on March 26, 1963){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Fine Arts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201090648/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html |archivedate=February 1, 2016|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. * Goyotome 42 Volumes - Records from the Edo to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Tanabe Town Ledger 130 Volumes and Town Ledger Quick Reference 8 Volumes - Records from the Momoyama to modern periods (books, designated on May 25, 1970). * Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala 1 Scroll - Painting. Designated on March 16, 2010. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Historic Site === * Tōkei Shrine Precincts - Designated on March 15, 2002{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=Tōkei Shrine (Shinkumano Tōkei Gongen Shrine) Precincts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. It is located at the western end of a series of small hills extending from the eastern part of the city, with the shrine buildings facing north. On the hillside from the middle to the top of Kariyanoyama behind the shrine, three Kofuns from the late Heian to early Kamakura periods were found, yielding artifacts such as jars, sutra cylinders, small boxes, knives, small inkstones, and ancient coins{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=Tōkei Shrine Precincts|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=February 14, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." Minakata was married to Matsue, the fourth daughter of the shrine's chief priest, Tamura Sozo. == Events == === festivals === * Ota festival ** April 15 * Summer Purification ceremony ** June 30{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Summer Purification ceremony |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} * festival ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) ** July 24 (Evening) ** July 25 (Main festival) {{main|Tanabe festival}} * Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ** December 31{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} === Other Events === * {{ill|Benkei festival|ja|弁慶まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (A play is performed at Tōkei Shrine on the first day of the festival, based on the legend that Musashibo Benkei was born at the Daifuku-in within the shrine precincts) ** Early October{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} Since October 1986 (Showa 61), the Benkei Market has been held at the Tōkei Shrine horse grounds (Higashi) on the third Sunday of each month to promote local products. In December 2020, the venue was moved to the Kappark at Oginoyama Park{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei Market |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }}[https://www.agara.co.jp/article/281766/ The famous morning market is popular - The Benkei Market in Tanabe has seen a 1.6-fold increase in visitors in one year] Kii Minpo, viewed June 18, 2023. == Parish Towns == {{main|Tanabe festival#Kasahoko and Kinasa}} {{main|Tanabe Castle#Castle Town}} * Honmachi * Egawacho * Fukurocho * Konyacho * Katamachi * Sakaemachi * Kitashimmachi * Minamishimmachi * Kamiyashikicho * Nakayashikicho * Shimoyashikicho * Arayashikicho * Imafuku * Egawamasugatamachi (Developed as a residential area during the Meiji and Taisho periods with land reclaimed from Egawahamacho) == Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range == : 4 {{ill|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - {{JIS2004|説明=雞}} {{神社 |名称=鬪雞神社 |画像=[[File:Tokei shrine torii.jpg|270px]]
鳥居
{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=270}} |所在地=[[和歌山県]][[田辺市]]東陽1-1 |ISO=JP-30 |緯度度=33|緯度分=43|緯度秒=46.9 |経度度=135|経度分=23|経度秒=2 |祭神=熊野三所神 |別名=闘鶏神社
田辺宮
新熊野
新熊野雞合大権現
権現さん |社格=旧[[県社]]・[[別表神社]] |創建=[[允恭天皇]]8年 |札所等=[[神仏霊場巡拝の道]]第5番（和歌山第5番） |例祭=[[7月24日]]・[[7月25日|25日]]（[[田辺祭]]） |地図=Japan Wakayama#Japan |本殿=春日造（本殿・上殿・八百萬殿）、四間社流造（中殿・下殿）入母屋造（西殿） }} '''鬪雞神社'''（とうけいじんじゃ）{{Cite web|和書|title=和歌山県神社庁-鬪鶏神社 とうけいじんじゃ-|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=7001|website=wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp|accessdate=2020-07-27}}{{Cite web|和書|title=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/midokoro/jinja/toukei/|website=田辺探訪（和歌山県田辺観光協会） :: 闘鶏神社|accessdate=2020-07-27|language=ja}}は、[[和歌山県]][[田辺市]]にある[[神社]]。史跡（和歌山県指定文化財）の名称としては「鬪雞神社」となっているが、[[宗教法人]]の名称としては漢字に「鳥」の入った「鬪鷄神社」である[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf 和歌山県報第2243号（9頁）] 和歌山県、2023-06-18閲覧。「闘鶏神社」などとも表記される。旧称は'''田辺宮'''、'''新熊野'''、'''新熊野雞合大権現'''。通称：権現さん。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === [[允恭天皇]]8年（[[419年]]）9月に[[分霊#勧請|勧請]]したとされるが、創建時の神社の歴史はよくわかっていない[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf 鬪雞神社の歴史と文化] 田辺市立田辺歴史民俗資料館、2023-06-18閲覧[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf 文化財センター季刊情報誌 風車 紀州の歴史と文化の風] 公益財団法人和歌山県文化財センター、2023-06-18閲覧。一方、天武天皇の時代の[[684年]]に建立されたとする記録も残る。また、[[田辺湾]]の[[神島 (和歌山県)|神島]]に神光が上がり、まず仮庵山（社殿南側にある山）に降り立ち、しばらくして龍仙山へ移りさらに天に上っていったという龍神信仰も残っている。以上から龍神信仰を元にした自然崇拝の祭祀の場所が次第に整えられたものとみられる。 === 中近世 === 『[[紀伊続風土記]]』や江戸時代の古文書によると、12世紀前半に[[熊野別当]]・[[湛快]]のときに熊野三所権現を勧請した。そして熊野別当家によって聖地として整備され「新熊野権現社」と称されるようになった。 社名は『[[平家物語]]』の故事（鶏合わせ神事）に由来している。『平家物語』などによれば、[[治承・寿永の乱]]（源平合戦）の時、熊野別当・[[湛増]]は社地の[[ニワトリ|鶏]]を紅白2色に分けて闘わせ、白の鶏が勝ったことから[[源氏]]に味方することを決め『平家物語』鶏合わせ（[[壇ノ浦の戦い|壇ノ浦合戦]]）のくだり、[[熊野水軍]]を率いて[[壇ノ浦]]へ出陣したという。この『平家物語』の故事から中世には「鶏合大権現」「鶏合宮」「鬪雞宮」とも称された。 鬪雞神社のある地は[[西国三十三所|西国三十三カ所巡礼]]の第一番札所の那智山寺（[[青岸渡寺]]）から第二番札所の[[紀三井寺]]までの中継地で、中世以降は参詣道や巡礼路の要衝となった。 しかし、15世紀末以降に二度の戦乱による焼失（明応年間及び天正年間）で荒廃し、完全な再建まで約150年を要した。慶長5年（1600年）に田辺領主となった浅野左衛門佐は新熊野権現の再興を図った。紀州徳川家の統治後は紀州藩付家老の安藤家の所領となり、元和5年（1619年）に[[安藤直次]]が田辺領主となった後は町衆からの深い信仰も集めて神社は再興を果たした。 === 近現代 === [[明治]]の[[神仏分離]]の際に「'''鬪雞神社'''」を正式な社名とした。 [[1871年]]（明治4年）に郷社（田辺県）、[[1873年]]（明治6年）に村社（和歌山県）、[[1881年]]（明治14年）2月には[[県社]]となっている。 [[1915年]]（[[大正]]4年）7月19日、[[朝香宮鳩彦王]]が御成毛利柴庵『皇室と紀伊』（1935年）346頁。。 [[1971年]]（[[昭和]]46年）7月に[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に加列されている。 [[2016年]]（[[平成]]28年）[[10月23日]]、[[第40回世界遺産委員会]]継続会議において、[[文化遺産 (世界遺産)|世界文化遺産]]「[[紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道]]」に追加登録された[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more 世界遺産への追加登録承認　闘鶏神社や八上王子跡など]紀伊民報 2016年6月11日。 なお[[プロ野球]]の独立リーグ、BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE（現・[[関西独立リーグ (2代目)]]）に[[2017年]]（[[平成]]29年）より加盟した和歌山ファイティングバーズ（現・[[和歌山ウェイブス]]）はこの神社が名の由来だった{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = 野球で地域盛り上げたい 田辺市に独立リーグ球団 | publisher = [[紀伊民報]] | date = 2016-06-10 | accessdate = 2016-06-26 }}。 == 熊野神社としての重要性 == 現存する社殿は近世の再建に係る6棟が揃って遺存するもので、仮庵山を背に北面して建ち、東より西へ西殿、本殿、上殿、中殿、下殿、八百萬殿の6棟が横一列に並ぶ。 建立年代は上殿が最も古く明暦4年（万治元年、1658年）に氏子衆によって建てられた。次いで上殿東側に本殿が[[寛文]]元年（[[1661年]]）に[[安藤直清]]によって寄進された。それから数十年後の[[元文]]2年（[[1737年]]）に本殿東側に西殿が再建された。さらに上殿西側の中殿（中四社）、下殿（下四社）、八百萬殿（満山宮）が[[延享]]5年（[[1748年]]）に再建されて社殿群6棟が揃った。本殿（證誠殿）と上殿（西御前）の配置は熊野本宮大社と共通しており、本殿の祭神が伊邪那美命である点が異なるが、当社には『那智参詣曼荼羅』が伝わるなど熊野との強い関係性を示している。 本殿と上殿は一間社[[春日造]]かつ奥行二間とする、いわゆる熊野造で田辺地方における数少ない17世紀中期以前に遡る貴重な神社建築例である。各棟ともに細部には地域的特色を備え、近世における当地方の神社建築の展開を考えるうえでも貴重な遺構とされる{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=鬪雞神社/６棟|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ わかやま文化財ガイド]|publisher=和歌山県|accessdate=2015-02-14}}。これらの社殿は国の重要文化財に指定されている。 == 祭神 == 社殿は6棟あり、それぞれ以下の神を祀る。 * 本殿 - 祭神：[[イザナミ|伊邪那美命]] * 西殿 - 祭神：速玉之男命、事解之男神 * 上殿 - 祭神：[[イザナギ|伊邪那岐命]]、[[天照大神|天照皇大神]]、[[ウカノミタマ|宇賀御魂命]] * 中殿 - 祭神：[[ニニギ|瓊々杵尊命]]、[[ウガヤフキアエズ|鵜葺草葺不合命]]、[[ホオリ|火々出見尊]]、[[アメノオシホミミ|天之忍穂耳命]] * 下殿 - 祭神：[[カグツチ|火産霊命]]、[[ミヅハノメ|弥都波能売命]]、[[ワクムスビ|稚産霊命]]、[[ハニヤス|埴山比売命]] * 八百萬殿 - 祭神：[[アメノタヂカラオ|手力男命]]、[[八百万の神|八百万神]] == 境内 == * 本殿（證誠殿、[[重要文化財]]） - [[寛文]]元年（[[1661年]]）建。熊野造。 * 西殿（重要文化財） - [[元文]]2年（[[1737年]]）建。 * 上殿（重要文化財） - 江戸時代前期建。熊野造。 * 中殿（重要文化財） - [[延享]]5年（[[1748年]]）建。 * 下殿（重要文化財） - 延享5年（1748年）建。 * 八百萬殿（重要文化財） - 延享5年（1748年）建。 * 拝殿 * 藤厳神社 - 祭神：[[安藤直次]]。[[紀伊田辺藩]]初代藩主で[[紀州藩]][[御附家老|附家老]]。 * 玉置神社 - 祭神：手置帆負命 * 雞姫弁財天社 - 祭神：[[イチキシマヒメ|市杵島姫命]] * 戎大黒神社 - 祭神：[[えびす|恵比寿]]、[[大黒天]] * 弁慶社 - 祭神：[[武蔵坊弁慶]] * 社務所 * 湛増・弁慶の像 * 境外社 ** [[稲荷神社]] ** [[八坂神社]] ** [[えびす神社|恵比須神社]] ** 弁天神社 ** 浦安神社 File:Tokei shrine Haiden.jpg|拝殿 File:Tokei shrine Nishi.jpg|西殿 File:Tokei shrine 1.jpg|社殿（手前から中殿・上殿・本殿・西殿） File:Tokei shrine 2.jpg|社殿（手前から中殿・下殿・八百萬殿） File:Tokei shrine ookusu.jpg|大楠 File:Tokei jinja kumano tanzou.JPG|湛増と弁慶の像 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財 === * 闘雞神社 6棟（建造物） *: 内訳は以下。[[2000年]]（[[平成]]21年）3月17日に「鬪雞神社 6棟」として和歌山県指定の[[有形文化財]]に指定されたのち{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=県指定文化財・有形文化財・建造物|publisher=和歌山県教育委員会|accessdate=2014-02-14}}、[[2017年]]（平成29年）2月23日に国の[[重要文化財]]に指定平成29年2月23日文部科学省告示第17号。。 ** 本殿（證誠殿） ** 西殿 ** 上殿 ** 中殿 ** 下殿 ** 八百萬殿 === 国の史跡 === * 史跡「[[熊野古道|熊野参詣道]]」の一部（[[2015年]]〈平成27年〉10月7日、追加指定）{{Cite web|和書|publisher=田辺市教育委員会|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=田辺市の指定文化財一覧表|accessdate=2016-05-20}}。 === 国の名勝 === * 名勝「南方曼荼羅の風景地」の一部（2015年〈平成27年〉10月7日指定）{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=田辺市の指定文化財一覧表|publisher=田辺市教育委員会|accessdate=2016-05-21}}。 === 和歌山県指定有形文化財 === * 万代記 1括 - 室町から江戸の記録。和歌山県指定有形文化財（書籍、[[1963年]]〈昭和38年〉3月26日指定）{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html|title=県指定文化財・有形文化財・美術工芸品|publisher=和歌山県教育委員会|accessdate=2014-02-14|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201090648/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenbizyutu.html |archivedate=2016-02-01|url-status=dead|url-status-date=2019-07}}。 * 御用留 42冊 - 江戸時代から近代の記録（書籍、[[1970年]]〈昭和45年〉5月25日指定）。 * 田辺町大帳 130冊および町大帳早引 8冊 - 桃山～近代の記録（書籍、1970年〈昭和45年〉5月25日指定）。 * [[那智参詣曼荼羅]] 1幅 - 絵画。[[2010年]]（平成22年）3月16日指定。 === 和歌山県指定史跡 === * 鬪雞神社境内 - [[2002年]]（平成23年）3月15日指定{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=鬪雞神社 （新熊野鬪雞権現社）境内|publisher=和歌山県教育委員会|accessdate=2014-02-14|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=2017-02-23|url-status=dead|url-status-date=2019-07}}。市街の東部に連なる小丘陵の西端、仮庵山の北麓にあり、社殿はほぼ北向きに鎮座している。社殿背後の仮庵山の中腹から山頂で、平安時代末期から鎌倉時代初頭の経塚が3基発見され、外容器の甕、経筒、合子（ごうす）、刀子（とうす）、小型硯、古銭などの遺物が出土した{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=鬪雞神社境内|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ |archivedate=2017-02-23|url-status=dead|url-status-date=2019-07}}。また、仮庵山については[[南方熊楠]]が「当県で平地にはちょっと見られぬ密林なり」と述べている。熊楠は闘雞神社[[宮司]]田村宗造の四女松枝の夫である。 == 行事 == === 祭事　=== * 御田祭 ** 4月15日 * 夏越大祓式 ** 6月30日{{Cite It is designated as a historic site under Wakayama Prefecture's cultural properties, and the religious corporation name includes "鳥" (chicken) as "鬪鷄神社"[https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/kenpou_bak/2011/201103_kenpou_d/fil/h2303252243.pdf Wakayama Prefecture Report No. 2243 (page 9)] Wakayama Prefecture, viewed June 18, 2023. It is also referred to as "Tōkei Shrine" and has various other names such as "Tanabe no Miya," "Shinkumano," "Shinkumano Niwatori Gongen," and "Gongen-san." The former shrine Rank is {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and it is currently listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == === Foundation === It is said that the shrine was founded in the 8th year of Emperor Ingyō (419), but the history of the shrine at its founding is not well known[https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/rekimin/files/R01kikaku1600-kaisai.pdf History and Culture of Tōkei Shrine] Tanabe City Historical and Folklore Museum, viewed June 18, 2023[http://www.wabunse.or.jp/publication/kazaguruma/pdf/kazaguruma94.pdf Quarterly Information Magazine of the Cultural Property Center, Kaza Guruma, History and Culture of Kishu] Public Interest Foundation Wakayama Prefecture Cultural Property Center, viewed June 18, 2023. There are also records that it was established in 684 during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Furthermore, there is a tradition of dragon deity worship based on the light of a god rising from Kamishima in Tanabe Bay, descending first to Kariyanoyama (a mountain south of the shrine), then to Ryusen'yama, and finally ascending to heaven. From this, it is thought that a place of worship based on dragon deity worship gradually developed into the shrine. === Middle and Early Modern Periods === According to the {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and ancient documents from the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to the Kumano Sansho Gongen during the time of the Kumano Betto, Tankai, in the early 12th century. It was then maintained as a sacred site by the Kumano Betto family and became known as "Shinkumano Gongen Shrine". The name of the shrine originates from the story in the {{ill|Heike Monogatari|ja|平家物語|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the tale of the cockfighting ritual). According to the Heike Monogatari and other sources, during the Genpei War (Jisho-Juei War), the Kumano Betto, Tanza, decided to support the Genji after witnessing a white rooster defeating a red rooster in a cockfight held at the shrine groundsHeike Monogatari, the episode of the cockfighting ritual (Taira no Kiyomori's War). He led the Kumano navy to the Battle of Dan-no-ura. This story led to the shrine being known as "Niwatori Gongen," "Niwatori no Miya," and "Tōkei no Miya" during the medieval period. The location of Tōkei Shrine became a key point on the pilgrimage route from the first sacred site of the {{ill|Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|西国三十三所|1=Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage|12=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at Nachisan-dera ({{ill|Seiganto-ji|ja|青岸渡寺|1=Seiganto-ji|12=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) to the second site at {{ill|Kimiidera|ja|紀三井寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} from the medieval period onwards. However, the shrine fell into disrepair after two periods of destruction by war in the late 15th century (during the Meio and Tensho periods), and it took about 150 years for it to be completely rebuilt. After becoming the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Keicho (1600), Asano Saemon-no-suke worked to revive Shinkumano Gongen. Under the rule of the Kishu Tokugawa family, it became the territory of the Ando family, the Kishu Tokugawa's attached vassal, and after Ando Naotsugu became the lord of Tanabe in the 5th year of Genna (1619), the shrine was restored with deep faith from the townspeople. === Modern and Contemporary Periods === During the Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the shrine was officially named "Tōkei Shrine". In 1871 (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine (Tanabe Prefecture), in 1873 (Meiji 6), a village shrine (Wakayama Prefecture), and in February 1881 (Meiji 14), a prefectural shrine. In July 1971 (Showa 46), it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On October 23, 2016 (Heisei 28), it was added to the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as a World Cultural Heritage site at the 40th Session of the World Heritage Committee[http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=316024&p=more Approved for addition to World Heritage Site - Tōkei Shrine and Yagami Shrine Ruins] Kii Minpo, June 11, 2016. The name of the professional baseball team in the independent league, BASEBALL FIRST LEAGUE (now {{ill|Kansai Independent Baseball League (second generation)|ja|関西独立リーグ (2代目)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), which joined in 2017 (Heisei 29), the Wakayama Fighting Birds (now {{ill|Wakayama Waves|ja|和歌山ウェイブス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), was derived from this shrine{{Cite news | url = http://www.agara.co.jp/news/daily/?i=315969&p=more | title = I want to excite the region with baseball - An independent league team in Tanabe City | publisher = Kii Minpo | date = June 10, 2016 | accessdate = June 26, 2016 }}. == Importance as a Kumano Shrine == The existing shrine buildings consist of six structures rebuilt during the early modern period, facing north with Kariyanoyama behind them. From east to west, the Western Hall, main hall, Upper Hall, Middle Hall, Lower Hall, and Yaoyorozu Hall are lined up in a row. The Upper Hall, built by the parishioners in the 4th year of Meireki (the first year of Manji, 1658), is the oldest. Next, the main hall to the east of the Upper Hall was donated by Ando Naotsugu in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Several decades later, the Western Hall to the east of the main hall was rebuilt in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). Furthermore, in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748), the Middle Hall (Nakashiya), Lower Hall (Shitashiya), and Yaoyorozu Hall (Manzangū) to the west of the Upper Hall were rebuilt, completing the six buildings. The layout of the main hall (Shōseidō) and Upper Hall (Nishimiya) is similar to that of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with the main difference being the deity enshrined in the main hall (Izanami). The shrine has a strong connection with Kumano, as evidenced by the transmission of the Nachi Pilgrimage Mandala. The main hall and Upper Hall are examples of the Kumano style with one-bay Kasuga-zukuri and a depth of two bays, representing the few remaining examples of 17th-century shrine architecture in the Tanabe area. Each building has regional characteristics, making them valuable structures for understanding the development of shrine architecture in the early modern period in this region{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi?action=view_id&view_id=541|title=Tōkei Shrine / 6 Buildings|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=2015-02-14}}. These buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan. == Deities == The shrine buildings include six structures, each enshrining the following deities: * main hall - deity: [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * Western Hall - Deities: Hayatama-no-Omikami, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami * Upper Hall - Deities: [[Izanagi|Izanagi-no-Mikoto]], [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu-Ōmikami]], Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto * Middle Hall - Deities: Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto, Amenooshihomimi-no-Mikoto * Lower Hall - Deities: Kagutsuchi-no-Mikoto, Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto, Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto, Haniyasu-hime-no-Mikoto * Yaoyorozu Hall - Deities: Tajikarao-no-Mikoto, Yaoyorozu-no-Kami == Precincts == * main hall (Shōseidō, Important Cultural Property) - Built in the first year of Kanbun (1661). Kumano style. * Western Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 2nd year of Genbun (1737). * Upper Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the early Edo period. Kumano style. * Middle Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Lower Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Yaoyorozu Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Built in the 5th year of Enkyo (1748). * Worship Hall * Fujikura Shrine - deity: Ando Naotsugu. Designated as tangible cultural properties of Wakayama Prefecture on March 17, 2000 (Heisei 21){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkenzo.html|title=Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties: Tangible Cultural Properties: Buildings|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014}}, and designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan on February 23, 2017 (Heisei 29)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 17, February 23, 2017.. ** main hall (Shōseidō) ** Western Hall ** Upper Hall ** Middle Hall ** Lower Hall ** Yaoyorozu Hall === National Historic Site === * Part of the historic site "Kumano Kodo" (additional designation on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|accessdate=May 20, 2016}}. === National Place of Scenic Beauty === * Part of the scenic beauty "Landscape of Southern Mandala" (designated on October 7, 2015){{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_ichiran.html|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=May 21, 2016}}. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Mandai-ki 1 Set - Records from the Muromachi to Edo periods. Designated on March 16, 2010. === Wakayama Prefecture-designated Historic Site === * Tōkei Shrine Precincts - Designated on March 15, 2002{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html|title=Tōkei Shrine (Shinkumano Tōkei Gongen Shrine) Precincts|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture Board of Education|accessdate=February 14, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125742/https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/shinshitei/h23/kenkinenbutu-h23.3.15-8.html |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. It is located at the western end of a series of small hills extending from the eastern part of the city, with the shrine buildings facing north. On the hillside from the middle to the top of Kariyanoyama behind the shrine, three Kofuns from the late Heian to early Kamakura periods were found, yielding artifacts such as jars, sutra cylinders, small boxes, knives, small inkstones, and ancient coins{{Cite web|和書|url=http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi|title=Tōkei Shrine Precincts|work=[http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/ Wakayama Cultural Property Guide]|publisher=Wakayama Prefecture|accessdate=February 14, 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223211439/http://wave.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/bunkazai/cgi/search.cgi |archivedate=February 23, 2017|deadlinkdate=July 2019}}. Minakata Kumagusu also noted that "there is a dense forest in this county that cannot be seen on the plains." Minakata was married to Matsue, the fourth daughter of the shrine's chief priest, Tamura Sozo. == Events == === festivals === * Ota festival ** April 15 * Summer Purification ceremony ** June 30{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Summer Purification ceremony |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} * festival ({{ill|Tanabe festival|ja|田辺祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) ** July 24 (Evening) ** July 25 (Main festival) {{main|Tanabe festival}} * Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ** December 31{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Year-end Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} === Other Events === * {{ill|Benkei festival|ja|弁慶まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (A play is performed at Tōkei Shrine on the first day of the festival, based on the legend that Musashibo Benkei was born at the Daifuku-in within the shrine precincts) ** Early October{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/kouhou/tanabe31/files/kt201906p0207.pdf |title=Benkei festival |publisher=Tanabe City |work= Learning about Tōkei Shrine |accessdate=April 20, 2020 }} Since October 1986 (Showa 61), the Benkei Market has been held at the Tōkei Shrine horse grounds (Higashi) on the third Sunday of each month to promote local products.
